summary: The note describes the British five pound (£5) coin, a commemorative denomination of the pound sterling. Its obverse has shown Queen Elizabeth II since its introduction in 1990, with two different portraits used, the latest by Ian Rank-Broadley introduced in 1998. Unlike standard coins, it has no fixed reverse and its design changes yearly to commemorate events.
one_line: Overview of the British £5 commemorative coin, its Queen Elizabeth II obverse portraits, and its yearly changing reverse designs.
key_facts: The British five pound (£5) coin is a commemorative denomination of the pound sterling.
The obverse of the British five pound coin has featured the profile of Queen Elizabeth II since the coin's introduction in 1990.
Two different portraits of Queen Elizabeth II have appeared on the British five pound coin.
The latest portrait on the British five pound coin is by Ian Rank-Broadley and was introduced in 1998.
The British five pound coin has no standard reverse design.
The reverse of the British five pound coin is altered each year to commemorate important events.
Variant obverses have been used on the British five pound coin on occasion.
